title: CMS Medicaid/CHIP enrollment, Mar 2026
question: What will CMS first publish as total Medicaid and CHIP enrollment for March 2026 in the preliminary March 2026 Applications, Eligibility, and Enrollment Data fixed vintage?
resolutionSource: Official CMS Medicaid.gov monthly Medicaid and CHIP enrollment data release
resolutionRule: Resolve to the whole-number Total Medicaid and CHIP Enrollment count in CMS's first official Preliminary March 2026 Applications, Eligibility, and Enrollment Data fixed vintage linked from Medicaid.gov and hosted on data.medicaid.gov. Do not use later updated March 2026 data or revisions. If CMS publishes state rows only, sum the official state-level Total Medicaid and CHIP Enrollment counts in that preliminary March 2026 vintage, preserving CMS whole-count precision.

reasoning.text: Base rate: the comparable preliminary series was falling by about 128,000 to 156,000 per month across the latest three month-to-month moves, far below the steep unwinding losses of 2023-2024.

reasoning.call: Checked the official monthly page for adjacent releases around the target month.
reasoning.result: The same official release list showed February 2026 preliminary and updated entries, January 2026 preliminary and updated entries, and the March 2026 preliminary entry, all with June 26, 2026 visible on the page.

reasoning.text: Level and momentum: starting from 78,184,000 in February, I use a judgmental inside-view adjustment that keeps the decline slightly milder than the recent -145,000 average because the latest move was the smallest of the three fetched changes at about -128,000.

Policy and one-off mechanisms: upside would come from late state processing stabilization, continuous-eligibility effects, or stronger CHIP retention; downside would come from renewal backlogs, eligibility redeterminations, and state reporting corrections hitting the preliminary count.

Recent monthly declines were roughly -152,000, -156,000, and -128,000, with an average near -145,000. I use a milder March decline of -124,000 from 78,184,000, giving 78,060,000. The 80% interval is about 5.6 times the recent average absolute one-month move to allow for state reporting dispersion and first-print noise: 78,060,000 - 810,000 = 77,250,000 and 78,060,000 + 840,000 = 78,900,000.

Counter-consideration: if preliminary March captures more retroactive or late-processed enrollment than usual, the print could sit above February despite the broader downward trend; conversely, a cluster of state methodology changes could push the count below the interval.

Outside-the-interval scenarios: below 77,250,000 would likely require unusually broad renewal-related terminations or a reporting break; above 78,900,000 would likely require a material state resubmission effect or a broad March enrollment rebound.

Review disposition: accepted the resolver-date critique by tying resolution to the official March 2026 preliminary link dated June 26, 2026; accepted the interval critique by making the recent-change basis explicit; accepted the update critique by labeling the milder decline as a judgmental adjustment from the latest observed momentum.
